answer: Each identity commissions synthesis of a 120-base DNA strand whose sequence is seeded by its key and logged under a sable registry tag. Monthly, an accredited lab sequences a fresh sample and posts the read hash; a mismatch, or one read serving two identities, revokes the slot. Making 1,000 fakes means 1,000 distinct synthesis orders at $85 each plus $40 per sequencing check ($125,000 yearly), since copying one strand only reproduces its own sequence, like stars copied from one nebula point. Trade-off: labs must screen orders for hazards and karst-region agents face slow shipping.
